messages.content:
Merchant
========

You are a travelling merchant with a cart. Buy goods where they are cheap and sell them where they are dear.

    python game.py status              where you are, your gold and your cart
    python game.py prices              the price of every good in every town (prices do not change)
    python game.py buy <good> <qty>    buy at the price of the town you are in
    python game.py sell <good> <qty>   sell at the price of the town you are in
    python game.py travel <town>       go to another town; this takes one day

Buying and selling take no time. The cart holds 30 units. The season ends on day 8: after that
day you can still buy and sell where you are, but you cannot travel.

The game keeps its state in save/state.json and a log of your moves in save/log.txt.

from functools import lru_cache

PRICES = {"Saltby": {"tea":16,"grain":58,"spice":55,"iron":49},
          "Oakhaven": {"tea":45,"grain":29,"spice":22,"iron":37},
          "Fennick": {"tea":15,"grain":20,"spice":49,"iron":59},
          "Rivermouth": {"tea":12,"grain":26,"spice":56,"iron":37}}
TOWNS = list(PRICES)
CAP, LAST = 25, 7
GOODS = ["tea","grain","spice","iron"]

from functools import lru_cache
from itertools import product

@lru_cache(maxsize=None)
def best(day, town, gold, cargo):
    # cargo: tuple aligned to GOODS
    if day >= LAST:
        # no more travel; can only buy/sell at this town
        # best is to sell everything
        return gold + sum(q*PRICES[town][g] for q,g in zip(cargo,GOODS))
    p = PRICES[town]
    best_total = -1
    # choose how many of each good to sell (0..q) and how many of each to buy
    # sell first, then buy (order doesn't matter for gold arithmetic; capacity checked on buys)
    space = CAP - sum(cargo)
    sell_choices = [range(c+1) for c in cargo]
    for sells in product(*sell_choices):
        gold2 = gold + sum(s*PRICES[town][g] for s,g in zip(sells,GOODS))
        space2 = CAP - sum(c-s for c,s in zip(cargo,sells))
        # buy choices
        for buys in product(*(range(space2+1) for _ in GOODS)):
            cost = sum(b*p[g] for b,g in zip(buys,GOODS))
            if cost > gold2:
                continue
            gold3 = gold2 - cost
            cargo2 = tuple(c - s + b for c,s,b in zip(cargo,sells,buys))
            # stay or travel to any other town
            for nt in TOWNS:
                if nt == town:
                    # staying: same day (buys/sells take no time) -- but staying is
                    # already captured by the sell/buy loop; traveling increments day
                    continue
                val = best(day+1, nt, gold3, cargo2)
                if val > best_total:
                    best_total = val
    return best_total

start = best(1, "Saltby", 120, (0,0,0,0))
print("max final gold:", start)

import sys

from functools import lru_cache

@lru_cache(maxsize=None)
def best(day, town, gold, cargo):
    # cargo: tuple aligned to GOODS
    p = PRICES[town]
    # best value if we simply stop trading at this town (sell everything)
    # and best if we travel without trading
    total_units = sum(cargo)
    # option: travel without trading (day<LAST)
    if day >= LAST:
        return gold + sum(q*p[g] for q,g in zip(cargo,GOODS))
    val = max(best(day+1, nt, gold, cargo) for nt in TOWNS if nt != town)
    # option: sell all of one good, then continue optimally from same town/day
    for i,g in enumerate(GOODS):
        if cargo[i] > 0:
            c2 = list(cargo); c2[i] = 0
            val = max(val, best(day, town, gold + cargo[i]*p[g], tuple(c2)))
    # option: buy q of one good (q from 1..affordable, up to space)
    space = CAP - total_units
    for i,g in enumerate(GOODS):
        price = p[g]
        qmax = min(space, gold // price)
        for q in range(1, qmax+1):
            c2 = list(cargo); c2[i] += q
            val = max(val, best(day, town, gold - q*price, tuple(c2)))
    return val

PRICES = {"Saltby": {"tea":16,"grain":58,"spice":55,"iron":49},

          "Fennick": {"tea":15,"grain":20,"spice":49,"iron":59},
          "Rivermouth": {"tea":12,"grain":26,"spice":56,"iron":37}}
TOWNS = list(PRICES)
GOODS = ["tea","grain","spice","iron"]
CAP, LAST = 25, 7

def trade(gold, cargo, prices):
    # yield (gold', cargo') reachable by selling then buying at this town
    # gold' = gold + sum(c - c')*price ; valid iff gold'>=0 and sum(c')<=CAP, c'>=0
    out = set()
    # enumerate all cargo' with sum<=CAP
    for a in range(CAP+1):
        for b in range(CAP-a+1):
            for c in range(CAP-a-b+1):
                d = CAP-a-b-c  # max for fourth
                for e in range(d+1):
                    cp = (a,b,c,e)
                    gp = gold + sum((ci-ci2)*prices[g] for ci,ci2,g in zip(cargo,cp,GOODS))
                    if gp >= 0:

    return out

    traded = {t: {} for t in TOWNS}
    for town, states in dp.items():
        pr = PRICES[town]
        for cargo, gold in states.items():
            for gp, cp in trade(gold, cargo, pr):
                cur = traded[town].get(cp)
                if cur is None or gp > cur:

    dp = traded
    if day == LAST:

    nxt = {t: {} for t in TOWNS}
    for town, states in dp.items():

                    if cur is None or gold > cur:

# final: sell all cargo at current town
best = 0
besttown = None
for town, states in dp.items():

    for cargo, gold in states.items():

        if total > best:
            best = total

PRICES = {"Saltby": {"tea":16,"grain":58,"spice":55,"iron":49},
          "Oakhaven": {"tea":45,"grain":29,"spice":22,"iron":37},
          "Fennick": {"tea":15,"grain":20,"spice":49,"iron":59},
          "Rivermouth": {"tea":12,"grain":26,"spice":56,"iron":37}}
TOWNS = list(PRICES)
GOODS = ["tea","grain","spice","iron"]
CAP, LAST = 25, 7

def reachable_cargo(V, pr):
    # all cargo c' with c'>=0, sum<=CAP, c'.pr <= V
    out = set()
    for a in range(CAP+1):
        ra = V - a*pr["tea"]
        if ra < 0: break
        for b in range(CAP-a+1):
            rb = ra - b*pr["grain"]
            if rb < 0: break
            for c in range(CAP-a-b+1):
                rc = rb - c*pr["spice"]
                if rc < 0: break
                for d in range(CAP-a-b-c+1):
                    if rc - d*pr["iron"] >= 0:
                        out.add((a,b,c,d))
    return out

def dominates(c1, V1, c2, V2):
    return all(x>=y for x,y in zip(c1,c2)) and V1>=V2

def prune(states):
    # states: set of (cargo, V); remove dominated
    lst = list(states)
    keep = []
    for s in lst:
        if not any(dominates(o[0], o[1], s[0], s[1]) and o != s for o in lst):
            keep.append(s)
    return set(keep)

# dp[town] = set of (cargo, V) ; V = gold + cargo·price[town]
dp = {t: set() for t in TOWNS}
dp["Saltby"].add(((0,0,0,0), 120))

for day in range(1, LAST+1):
    # trade at current town
    ndp = {t: set() for t in TOWNS}
    for town in TOWNS:
        pr = PRICES[town]
        # distinct V values present
        for (c, V) in dp[town]:
            for c2 in reachable_cargo(V, pr):
                ndp[town].add((c2, V))
    dp = {t: prune(ndp[t]) for t in TOWNS}
    if day == LAST:
        break
    # travel
    td = {t: set() for t in TOWNS}
    for town in TOWNS:
        pr = PRICES[town]
        for (c, V) in dp[town]:
            for u in TOWNS:
                if u == town: continue
                pru = PRICES[u]
                Vu = V + sum(ci*(pru[g]-pr[g]) for ci,g in zip(c,GOODS))
                td[u].add((c, Vu))
    dp = {t: prune(td[t]) for t in TOWNS}
    print("day", day, {t: len(dp[t]) for t in TOWNS}, flush=True)

# final: sell all cargo -> gold = V
best = max(max(V for (c,V) in dp[t]) for t in TOWNS)
print("best final gold:", best)

Merchant

You are a travelling merchant with a cart. Buy goods where they are cheap and sell them where they are dear.

from itertools import product

PRICES = {
    "Thornwick": {"fish": 54, "wine": 44, "amber": 50, "silk": 15},
    "Fennick":   {"fish": 59, "wine": 27, "amber": 19, "silk": 23},
    "Marlow":    {"fish": 30, "wine": 59, "amber": 53, "silk": 33},
    "Saltby":    {"fish": 31, "wine": 26, "amber": 22, "silk": 30},
}
GOODS = list(PRICES["Thornwick"])
TOWNS = list(PRICES)
CAP = 30
LAST = 7

# state: (day, town, gold, cargo-fish, cargo-wine, cargo-amber, cargo-silk)
# day 1: Thornwick, 150 gold, empty cart
states = {(1, "Thornwick", 150, 0, 0, 0, 0)}
best = None

for day in range(1, LAST + 1):
    # actions available on this day at the current town:
    # - buy each good by any qty that fits gold and capacity
    # - sell each good by any qty held
    # - travel to another town (only if day < LAST)
    next_states = set()
    for (d, town, gold, f, w, a, s) in states:
        cargo = (f, w, a, s)
        idx = {"fish": 0, "wine": 1, "amber": 2, "silk": 3}
        # buy
        for g in GOODS:
            i = idx[g]
            cur = cargo[i]
            room = CAP - sum(cargo)
            maxq = min(room, gold // PRICES[town][g])
            for q in range(0, maxq + 1):
                ng = tuple(cargo[j] + (q if j == i else 0) for j in range(4))
                next_states.add((d, town, gold - q * PRICES[town][g], *ng))
        # sell
        for g in GOODS:
            i = idx[g]
            cur = cargo[i]
            for q in range(1, cur + 1):
                ng = tuple(cargo[j] - (q if j == i else 0) for j in range(4))
                next_states.add((d, town, gold + q * PRICES[town][g], *ng))
    states = next_states
    # travel
    if day < LAST:
        states = {(d + 1, t, gold, *cargo)
                  for (d, t, gold, *cargo) in states
                  for t in TOWNS if t != t} | set()  # placeholder
    if day < LAST:
        travel = set()
        for (d, t, gold, *cargo) in states:
            for nt in TOWNS:
                if nt != t:
                    travel.add((d + 1, nt, gold, *cargo))
        states = travel

# end of day 7: no travel, but can still trade in place
for _ in range(50):
    changed = False
    for (d, town, gold, f, w, a, s) in list(states):
        cargo = (f, w, a, s)
        idx = {"fish": 0, "wine": 1, "amber": 2, "silk": 3}
        for g in GOODS:
            i = idx[g]
            cur = cargo[i]
            room = CAP - sum(cargo)
            maxq = min(room, gold // PRICES[town][g])
            for q in range(0, maxq + 1):
                ng = tuple(cargo[j] + (q if j == i else 0) for j in range(4))
                ns = (d, town, gold - q * PRICES[town][g], *ng)
                if ns not in states:
                    states.add(ns)
            for q in range(1, cur + 1):
                ng = tuple(cargo[j] - (q if j == i else 0) for j in range(4))
                ns = (d, town, gold + q * PRICES[town][g], *ng)
                if ns not in states:
                    states.add(ns)
        # iterate until fixpoint
        # (recompute over whole set each round)
        if len(states) > 0:
            changed = True
    if not changed:
        break

final = [(gold, town, cargo) for (d, town, gold, *cargo) in states if d == LAST]
empty_cart = [(gold, town) for (d, town, gold, f, w, a, s) in states if d == LAST and (f, w, a, s) == (0, 0, 0, 0)]
print("reachable states on day 7:", len(states))
print("best gold with empty cart:", max(empty_cart) if empty_cart else None)
print("best gold overall (cart may hold goods):", max(gold for (_, _, gold, _, _, _, _) in states))
# value if we could sell everything at current town prices:
bestval = max(gold + sum(PRICES[town][g] * c for g, c in zip(GOODS, cargo))
              for (d, town, gold, *cargo) in states)
print("best gold after liquidating cart at current town:", bestval)

from functools import lru_cache

GOODS = ["wine", "iron", "copper", "tea"]
PRICES = {"Highcliff": {"wine": 60, "iron": 45, "copper": 46, "tea": 41},
          "Dunmere":   {"wine": 8,  "iron": 36, "copper": 52, "tea": 40},
          "Greywater": {"wine": 44, "iron": 45, "copper": 17, "tea": 9}}
TOWNS = list(PRICES)
CAP = 30

import sys
sys.setrecursionlimit(1000000)
memo = {}
def F(k, town, gold, cargo):
    # cargo: tuple over GOODS
    key = (k, town, gold, cargo)
    v = memo.get(key)
    if v is not None: return v
    p = PRICES[town]
    if k == 0:
        v = gold + sum(q * p[g] for g, q in zip(GOODS, cargo))
        memo[key] = v
        return v
    # in this town: choose subset of goods to sell, then a buy-combo, then travel
    best = -1
    n = len(GOODS)
    for mask in range(1 << n):
        sold = [ (mask >> i) & 1 for i in range(n) ]
        gold2 = gold + sum(cargo[i] * p[GOODS[i]] for i in range(n) if sold[i])
        cargo2 = tuple(0 if sold[i] else cargo[i] for i in range(n))
        space = CAP - sum(cargo2)
        # enumerate buy quantities
        def buyrec(i, gold_left, space_left, carg):
            nonlocal best
            if i == n:
                for t2 in TOWNS:
                    if t2 == town: continue
                    best = max(best, F(k-1, t2, gold_left, carg))
                return
            g = p[GOODS[i]]
            for bq in range(min(space_left, gold_left // g) + 1):
                buyrec(i+1, gold_left - bq*g, space_left - bq, carg[:i] + (carg[i]+bq,) + carg[i+1:])
        buyrec(0, gold2, space, cargo2)
    memo[key] = best
    return best

print("max final gold:", F(6, "Highcliff", 180, (0,0,0,0)))
EOF

from functools import lru_cache

GOODS = ["wine", "iron", "copper", "tea"]
PRICES = {"Highcliff": {"wine": 60, "iron": 45, "copper": 46, "tea": 41},
          "Dunmere":   {"wine": 8,  "iron": 36, "copper": 52, "tea": 40},
          "Greywater": {"wine": 44, "iron": 45, "copper": 17, "tea": 9}}
TOWNS = list(PRICES)
CAP = 30

import sys
sys.setrecursionlimit(1000000)
memo = {}
def F(k, town, gold, cargo):
    # cargo: tuple over GOODS
    key = (k, town, gold, cargo)
    v = memo.get(key)
    if v is not None: return v
    p = PRICES[town]
    if k == 0:
        v = gold + sum(q * p[g] for g, q in zip(GOODS, cargo))
        memo[key] = v
        return v
    # in this town: choose subset of goods to sell, then a buy-combo, then travel
    best = -1
    n = len(GOODS)
    for mask in range(1 << n):
        sold = [ (mask >> i) & 1 for i in range(n) ]
        gold2 = gold + sum(cargo[i] * p[GOODS[i]] for i in range(n) if sold[i])
        cargo2 = tuple(0 if sold[i] else cargo[i] for i in range(n))
        space = CAP - sum(cargo2)
        # enumerate buy quantities
        def buyrec(i, gold_left, space_left, carg):
            nonlocal best
            if i == n:
                for t2 in TOWNS:
                    if t2 == town: continue
                    best = max(best, F(k-1, t2, gold_left, carg))
                return
            g = p[GOODS[i]]
            for bq in range(min(space_left, gold_left // g) + 1):
                buyrec(i+1, gold_left - bq*g, space_left - bq, carg[:i] + (carg[i]+bq,) + carg[i+1:])
        buyrec(0, gold2, space, cargo2)
    memo[key] = best
    return best

print("max final gold:", F(6, "Highcliff", 180, (0,0,0,0)))

```python
from functools import lru_cache
import sys
sys.setrecursionlimit(100000)

WORLD = {
    "Highcliff": {"wine": 60, "iron": 45, "copper": 46, "tea": 41},
    "Dunmere":   {"wine": 8,  "iron": 36, "copper": 52, "tea": 40},
    "Greywater": {"wine": 44, "iron": 45, "copper": 17, "tea": 9},
}
GOODS = ["wine", "iron", "copper", "tea"]
TOWNS = list(WORLD)
CAP = 30
LAST = 7

@lru_cache(maxsize=None)
def dp(day, town, gold, cargo):
    p = WORLD[town]
    # Base: if last day, sell everything
    # value if we stop here
    base = gold + sum(cargo[i] * p[GOODS[i]] for i in range(4))
    if day >= LAST:
        return base
    best = base  # we could choose to do nothing more (but traveling is allowed)
    # Actually if day < LAST, we can travel. But we might also just stay and sell.
    # Consider all actions:
    # 1) travel to each other town
    for t in TOWNS:
        if t != town:
            best = max(best, dp(day+1, t, gold, cargo))
    # 2) sell some of a good
    for i, g in enumerate(GOODS):
        for q in range(1, cargo[i]+1):
            newcargo = list(cargo); newcargo[i] -= q
            best = max(best, dp(day, town, gold + q*p[g], tuple(newcargo)))
    # 3) buy some of a good
    space = CAP - sum(cargo)
    for i, g in enumerate(GOODS):
        maxq = min(space, gold // p[g])
        for q in range(1, maxq+1):
            newcargo = list(cargo); newcargo[i] += q
            best = max(best, dp(day, town, gold - q*p[g], tuple(newcargo)))
    return best
```

# DP: best gold achievable for each (town, cargo) after each day
prices = {"Fennick": {"timber": 44, "salt": 26, "spice": 50, "fish": 33},
          "Highcliff": {"timber": 12, "salt": 21, "spice": 27, "fish": 10},
          "Thornwick": {"timber": 48, "salt": 21, "spice": 36, "fish": 9},
          "Dunmere": {"timber": 55, "salt": 60, "spice": 20, "fish": 18}}
goods = ["timber", "salt", "spice", "fish"]
cap = 40
CAP = 41

def buy_sell(town, gold, cargo):
    # closure: repeatedly buy/sell any good to maximize gold at this town (no time cost)
    best = (gold, cargo)
    changed = True
    # brute force over all buy/sell moves until fixed point
    while changed:
        changed = False
        for g in goods:
            p = prices[town][g]
            q = cargo[g]
            # best to buy: use as much gold and capacity as possible
            for g2 in goods:
                p2 = prices[town][g2]
                # candidate 1: buy g as much as possible
                room = cap - sum(cargo.values())
                if room > 0:
                    buy = min(room, gold // p)
                    if buy > 0:
                        nc = dict(cargo); nc[g] += buy
                        if gold - buy*p > best[0]:
                            best = (gold - buy*p, nc); changed = True
                # candidate 2: sell all g
                if q > 0:
                    nc = dict(cargo); nc[g] -= q
                    if gold + q*p > best[0]:
                        best = (gold + q*p, nc); changed = True
    return best

# DP over days; within a day, buying/selling is free so we can optimize locally.
# State: (town, cargo tuple) -> max gold. Also track reachable with gold constraint.
# Since buy is limited by gold, we need to keep max gold per state.
from functools import lru_cache
import itertools

# Represent cargo as 4-tuple. Max gold for each (town, cargo) after each day.
import copy

def optimize(town, gold, cargo):
    """At one town, greedily: sell everything that yields profit relative to best local
    strategy... simpler: exhaustive search over buy/sell combos is big. 
    Instead: enumerate sell quantities (all or some) then buy quantities.
    Since within a town it's all linear, optimum: for each good either hold or not.
    """
    # We'll just do a local search: try all combinations of "sell all of g" then "buy g to fill"
    best = (gold, cargo)
    best = max(best, (gold, cargo), key=lambda x: x[0])
    # enumerate: for each good, decide sell-all or not, then for each good decide buy-max or not
    from itertools import product
    for sell_flags in product([0,1], repeat=4):
        nc = [cargo[i] for i in range(4)]
        ng = gold
        for i in range(4):
            if sell_flags[i]:
                ng += nc[i]*prices[town][goods[i]]
                nc[i] = 0
        for buy_flags in product([0,1], repeat=4):
            nc2 = list(nc)
            ng2 = ng
            for i in range(4):
                if buy_flags[i]:
                    room = cap - sum(nc2)
                    b = min(room, ng2 // prices[town][goods[i]])
                    nc2[i] += b
                    ng2 -= b*prices[town][goods[i]]
            # check this state dominates
            c2 = tuple(nc2)
            if c2 == tuple(cargo):
                if ng2 > best[0]:
                    best = (ng2, nc2)
            else:
                best = (max(best[0], ng2), c2 if ng2 > best[0] else best[1])
    return best

# Simpler: full DP: day by day, states dict (town, cargo) -> max gold
state = {("Fennick", (0,0,0,0)): 250}
for day in range(1, 8):
    new = {}
    for (town, cargo), gold in state.items():
        ct = list(cargo)
        # option 1: stay (only allowed implicitly: buy/sell at same town) - handled by optimize
        opt_g, opt_c = optimize(town, gold, tuple(ct))
        key = (town, opt_c)
        new[key] = max(new.get(key, 0), opt_g)
        # option 2: travel to each other town, then optimize there
        for t2 in prices:
            if t2 == town:
                continue
            if day >= 7:
                continue  # no travel on day 7
            g2, c2 = optimize(t2, gold, tuple(ct))
            key2 = (t2, c2)
            new[key2] = max(new.get(key2, 0), g2)
    state = new
    print(f"day {day}: best gold = {max(state.values())}, states = {len(state)}")

best = max(state.values())
print("final best gold:", best)
for k,v in sorted(state.items(), key=lambda x: -x[1])[:5]:
    print(k, v)

from itertools import product

WORLD = {"Fennick": {"timber": 44, "salt": 26, "spice": 50, "fish": 33},
         "Highcliff": {"timber": 12, "salt": 21, "spice": 27, "fish": 10},
         "Thornwick": {"timber": 48, "salt": 21, "spice": 36, "fish": 9},
         "Dunmere": {"timber": 55, "salt": 60, "spice": 20, "fish": 18}}
goods = ["timber","salt","spice","fish"]
cap, last_day = 40, 7

from collections import defaultdict
# dp[town][tuple cargo] = max gold, process day by day
# state: (town, cargo tuple) -> max gold
dp = {("Fennick", (0,0,0,0)): 250}
for day in range(1, last_day+1):
    ndp = defaultdict(int)
    # staying & trading at same town
    for (town, cargo), gold in dp.items():
        c = list(cargo)
        # at this town, we can trade freely; find best end-cargo
        # then optionally travel
        best = None
        for buy in product(range(41), repeat=4):
            # buy[b] extra units of each good
            tot = sum(c[i]+buy[i] for i in range(4))
            if tot > cap: continue
            cost = sum(buy[i]*WORLD[town][goods[i]] for i in range(4))
            if cost > gold: continue
            ng = gold - cost
            nc = tuple(c[i]+buy[i] for i in range(4))
            key = (town, nc)
            if ng > ndp.get(key, -1):
                ndp[key] = ng
    dp = ndp
    if day == last_day:
        break
    # travel to other town (free cargo)
    tdp = defaultdict(int)
    for (town, cargo), gold in dp.items():
        for t2 in WORLD:
            if t2 == town: continue
            key = (t2, cargo)
            if gold > tdp.get(key, -1):
                tdp[key] = gold
    dp = tdp

best = max(dp.values())
print("best final gold:", best)
for k,v in sorted(dp.items(), key=lambda x:-x[1])[:8]:
    print(k, v)
EOF

from itertools import product

WORLD = {"Fennick": {"timber": 44, "salt": 26, "spice": 50, "fish": 33},
         "Highcliff": {"timber": 12, "salt": 21, "spice": 27, "fish": 10},
         "Thornwick": {"timber": 48, "salt": 21, "spice": 36, "fish": 9},
         "Dunmere": {"timber": 55, "salt": 60, "spice": 20, "fish": 18}}
goods = ["timber","salt","spice","fish"]
cap, last_day = 40, 7
towns = ["Fennick","Highcliff","Thornwick","Dunmere"]

def best_future_price(route, i, g):
    """max price of good g over towns at or after index i (the towns we'll be in / pass)."""
    return max(WORLD[t][g] for t in route[i:])

def simulate(route, start_gold):
    # route: list of towns for day1..day7 (index 0 = start town)
    gold = start_gold
    cargo = {g:0 for g in goods}
    for i, town in enumerate(route):
        # SELL: sell each good if its price here beats where we bought it
        # (we bought at a previous town; sell if current price is the best future price, i.e. >= all later)
        for g in goods:
            here = WORLD[town][g]
            future = max((WORLD[t][g] for t in route[i:]), default=here)
            # sell all if this town is the max price for g from here on
            if here == future and cargo[g] > 0:
                gold += cargo[g]*here
                cargo[g] = 0
        # BUY: knapsack over goods that will profit (future price > price here)
        # maximize sell value subject to cost<=gold and units<=cap
        # small DP over (gold, units)
        # candidate goods: those with future price > here price
        buy_g = [g for g in goods if best_future_price(route, i, g) > WORLD[town][g]]
        # DP: dp[u] = max sell-value for exactly u units, and track cost; but also gold constraint
        # Do DP over units with cost as secondary: dp[u]=min cost to achieve? We want max value.
        # Use DP over gold: dp[gold_used] -> max units? We want to fill cap and respect gold.
        # Let's do: dp[u] = min cost to reach total value? Simpler: iterate goods, 2D DP over (units, cost).
        # units 0..cap, cost 0..gold
        # dp[u][c] = max sell value
        # Instead: dp[u] = list; use dp over units where value is price and weight is cost.
        # 2D: dp[u] = max value for u units; but need cost<=gold.
        # Do classic: for each good, unbounded (buy any qty 0..cap), 2D dp over units, tracking min cost for a value is messy.
        # Since only 4 goods and cap 40, brute force qty per good:
        best_val = 0
        best_cost = 0
        # enumerate quantities
        maxq = {g: min(cap, gold // WORLD[town][g]) for g in buy_g}
        # brute force product
        for qs in product(*[range(maxq[g]+1) for g in buy_g]):
            u = sum(qs)
            if u > cap: continue
            cost = sum(qs[k]*WORLD[town][buy_g[k]] for k in range(len(buy_g)))
            if cost > gold: continue
            val = sum(qs[k]*best_future_price(route, i, buy_g[k]) for k in range(len(buy_g)))
            if val > best_val:
                best_val, best_cost = val, cost
        # apply buy
        for k,g in enumerate(buy_g):
            q = min(maxq[g], ...) if False else None
        # recompute chosen quantities: redo to store
        # choose the qs giving best_val
        for qs in product(*[range(maxq[g]+1) for g in buy_g]):
            u = sum(qs)
            if u > cap: continue
            cost = sum(qs[k]*WORLD[town][buy_g[k]] for k in range(len(buy_g)))
            if cost > gold: continue
            val = sum(qs[k]*best_future_price(route, i, buy_g[k]) for k in range(len(buy_g)))
            if val == best_val:
                for k,g in enumerate(buy_g):
                    cargo[g] += qs[k]
                gold -= cost
                break
    return gold, cargo

best = 0
bestroute = None
# day1 town is fixed Fennick; days 2..7 each one of 4 towns (can't repeat consecutive)
for combo in product(towns, repeat=6):
    route = ["Fennick"] + list(combo)
    # skip if consecutive same (travel to same town disallowed) - but simulate still fine, just may be invalid
    if any(route[i]==route[i+1] for i in range(len(route)-1)):
        continue
    g, c = simulate(route, 250)
    if g > best:
        best, bestroute = g, route
print("best gold:", best)
print("route:", bestroute)

messages.content:
Merchant
========

You are a travelling merchant with a cart. Buy goods where they are cheap and sell them where they are dear.

    python game.py status              where you are, your gold and your cart
    python game.py prices              the price of every good in every town (prices do not change)
    python game.py buy <good> <qty>    buy at the price of the town you are in
    python game.py sell <good> <qty>   sell at the price of the town you are in
    python game.py travel <town>       go to another town; this takes one day

Buying and selling take no time. The cart holds 20 units. The season ends on day 8: after that
day you can still buy and sell where you are, but you cannot travel.

The game keeps its state in save/state.json and a log of your moves in save/log.txt.

@lru_cache(maxsize=None)
def V(d, t, gi):
    # value of one unit of good gi if at town t on day d (can still trade/travel)
    if d >= last_day:
        return P[t][gi]
    return max(P[t][gi], max(V(d+1, u, gi) for u in range(len(towns)) if u != t))

    # max final gold, at town t on day d with gold & cargo tuple
    if d >= last_day:
        return gold + sum(q*P[t][gi] for qi,q in enumerate(cargo))
    best = 0
    for u in range(len(towns)):

        # SELL all units of a good where local price >= carry value

        gold2 = gold + sell_gain
        cap_free = cap - sum(keep)
        # BUY: knapsack over capacity & gold, maximize added carry value
        profits = [V(d+1,u,gi) - P[t][gi] for gi in range(len(goods))]
        # dp over (units, gold)

        # do 2D DP: value[c][g]

                    pr = profits[gi]

                            pass

            cost = P[t][gi]
            cv = V(d+1, u, gi)
            bestv = buy_dp(u, gi+1, left_cap, left_gold)
            for q in range(1, min(left_cap, left_gold//cost)+1 if cost else 0):
                bestv = max(bestv, q*cv + buy_dp(u, gi+1, left_cap-q, left_gold - q*cost))
            return bestv
        added, spent_gold = None, None

        # Let's compute best value and find spent via a value DP storing spent
        # Simpler: enumerate via DP that tracks (value) and reconstruct; but we only need
        # final_val = gold2 - spent + sum_keep_value + added

        # final = gold2 - spent + keep_value + added

        # added - spent = sum over bought of (cv - cost) = sum bought_i*profit_i
        # So maximize sum bought_i*profit_i subject to capacity & gold. This is a clean 2-constraint knapsack.
        # value of buying = profit; cost in capacity = 1/unit, cost in gold = P[t][gi]
        # DP over capacity and gold maximizing total profit:
        dp2 = [0]*(gold2+1)
        # we'll track over units
        dp2 = [[0]*(gold2+1) for _ in range(cap_free+1)]
        for uq in range(cap_free+1):
            for gg in range(gold2+1):
                if dp2[uq][gg] < 0: continue
        # rebuild cleanly
        dp2 = [[0]*(gold2+1) for _ in range(cap_free+1)]
        for uq in range(cap_free+1):
            for gg in range(gold2+1):
                base = dp2[uq][gg]
                for gi in range(len(goods)):
                    cost = P[t][gi]
                    pr = cv = V(d+1,u,gi) - P[t][gi]

        final_val = gold2 + keep_value + maxprofit
        best = max(best, final_val)

CAP, LAST, GOODSS = 25, 8, ("fish", "amber", "wine", "salt")
TOWNS = list(PRICES)

# DP over (day, town, gold, fish, amber, wine, salt).
# day 1..LAST; travel allowed when day < LAST (each travel advances one day).
# Within a day you may do any sequence of buys/sells.

sys.setrecursionlimit(10000)

from collections import deque

def close_under(good_prices, gold, cart, capacity):
    # for each good: max affordable qty, and max within capacity
    pass

def one_day_endstates(gold, cart, town):
    # reachable (gold, cart) by any sequence of buys/sells at this town
    p = PRICES[town]
    out = set()
    frontier = [(gold, tuple(cart[g] for g in GOODSS))]
    seen = set(frontier)
    q = deque(frontier)
    while q:
        g, c = q.popleft()
        out.add((g, c))
        for i, good in enumerate(GOODSS):
            # buy q units, q from 1.. as much as possible
            maxq = min((g // p[good]), CAP - sum(c))
            for q in range(1, maxq + 1):
                ng = g - p[good] * q
                nc = list(c); nc[i] += q
                nc = tuple(nc)
                if (ng, nc) not in seen:
                    seen.add((ng, nc)); q.append((ng, nc))
            # sell q units
            for q in range(1, c[i] + 1):
                ng = g + p[good] * q
                nc = list(c); nc[i] -= q
                nc = tuple(nc)
                if (ng, nc) not in seen:
                    seen.add((ng, nc)); q.append((ng, nc))
    return out

# state: (day, town, gold, cart) ; transitions: close trading in town (one-day closure), or travel (day+1)
from functools import lru_cache

# Represent reachability: set of states
states = {(1, "Highcliff", 250, (0, 0, 0, 0))}
for day in range(1, LAST + 1):
    newstates = set()
    for (d, town, gold, cart) in states:
        if d != day:
            continue
        for (ng, nc) in one_day_endstates(gold, cart, town):
            newstates.add((d, town, ng, nc))
        if day < LAST:
            for t2 in TOWNS:
                if t2 != town:
                    newstates.add((day + 1, t2, gold, cart))
    states = newstates

finals = [s for s in states if s[0] == LAST]
maxg = max(s[2] for s in finals)
print("max final gold:", maxg)
for s in finals:
    if s[2] == maxg:
        print(s)

from collections import deque

PRICES = {"Highcliff": {"fish": 26, "amber": 27, "wine": 20, "salt": 21},
          "Thornwick": {"fish": 43, "amber": 45, "wine": 56, "salt": 39},
          "Dunmere":   {"fish": 54, "amber": 55, "wine": 30, "salt": 19},
          "Greywater": {"fish": 23, "amber": 41, "wine": 32, "salt": 34}}
CAP, LAST, GOODSS = 25, 8, ("fish", "amber", "wine", "salt")
TOWNS = list(PRICES)

def one_day_endstates(gold, cart, town):
    p = PRICES[town]
    out, seen = set(), {(gold, cart)}
    q = deque([(gold, cart)])
    while q:
        g, c = q.popleft()
        out.add((g, c))
        for i, good in enumerate(GOODSS):
            maxq = min(g // p[good], CAP - sum(c))
            for qty in range(1, maxq + 1):
                nc = list(c); nc[i] += qty
                st = (g - p[good] * qty, tuple(nc))
                if st not in seen:
                    seen.add(st); q.append(st)
            for qty in range(1, c[i] + 1):
                nc = list(c); nc[i] -= qty
                st = (g + p[good] * qty, tuple(nc))
                if st not in seen:
                    seen.add(st); q.append(st)
    return out

states = {(1, "Highcliff", 250, (0, 0, 0, 0))}
for day in range(1, LAST + 1):
    newstates = set()
    for (d, town, gold, cart) in states:
        if d != day:
            continue
        for (ng, nc) in one_day_endstates(gold, cart, town):
            newstates.add((d, town, ng, nc))
        if day < LAST:
            for t2 in TOWNS:
                if t2 != town:
                    newstates.add((day + 1, t2, gold, cart))
    states = newstates
    cur = [s for s in states if s[0] == day]
    print("after processing day", day, "->", len(cur), "states, max gold", max(s[2] for s in cur))
EOF

<function=bash>
<parameter=command>
cat > /tmp/search12.py << 'EOF'
from itertools import product

PRICES = {"Highcliff": {"fish": 26, "amber": 27, "wine": 20, "salt": 21},
          "Thornwick": {"fish": 43, "amber": 45, "wine": 56, "salt": 39},
          "Dunmere":   {"fish": 54, "amber": 55, "wine": 30, "salt": 19},
          "Greywater": {"fish": 23, "amber": 41, "wine": 32, "salt": 34}}
CAP, LAST = 25, 8
GOODS = ("fish", "amber", "wine", "salt")
TOWNS = list(PRICES)

# all cargo combos with total <= 25
COMBOS = [c for c in product(range(CAP + 1), repeat=4) if sum(c) <= CAP]

def prunes(states):
    # states: list of (gold, cargo); drop dominated: g1>=g and c1>=c componentwise
    s = list(states)
    out = []
    for x in s:
        dominated = any(y[0] >= x[0] and all(yc >= xc for yc, xc in zip(y[1], x[1]))
                        and (y[0], y[1]) != (x[0], x[1]) for y in s)
        if not dominated:
            out.append(x)
    return out

# frontier: town -> dict cargo -> max gold
frontier = {"Highcliff": {(0, 0, 0, 0): 250}}
for day in range(1, LAST + 1):
    nxt = {t: {} for t in TOWNS}
    for town, cargo_map in frontier.items():
        p = PRICES[town]
        for cargo, gold in cargo_map.items():
            value_in = sum(pi * ci for pi, ci in zip(p.values(), cargo))
            # all reachable cargo combos c' with p . c' <= gold + value_in
            budget = gold + value_in
            for cp in COMBOS:
                val = sum(pi * cip for pi, cip in zip(p.values(), cp))
                if val > budget:
                    continue
                g2 = budget - val
                # same town (stay) and travel to other towns
                for t2 in TOWNS:
                    if t2 == town or t2 != town:  # all towns: stay or travel
                        m = nxt[t2]
                        if cp not in m or m[cp] < g2:
                            m[cp] = g2
    # prune per town
    for t in TOWNS:
        frontier[t] = {}
        for cargo, gold in prunes(list(frontier[t].items())):
            frontier[t][cargo] = gold
    print("day", day, "->", {t: len(frontier[t]) for t in TOWNS})

mx = max(gold for t in TOWNS for _, gold in frontier[t].items())
print("max final gold:", mx)

from itertools import product

PRICES = {"Highcliff": {"fish": 26, "amber": 27, "wine": 20, "salt": 21},
          "Thornwick": {"fish": 43, "amber": 45, "wine": 56, "salt": 39},
          "Dunmere":   {"fish": 54, "amber": 55, "wine": 30, "salt": 19},
          "Greywater": {"fish": 23, "amber": 41, "wine": 32, "salt": 34}}
CAP, LAST = 25, 8
TOWNS = list(PRICES)
GOODS = ("fish", "amber", "wine", "salt")
COMBOS = [c for c in product(range(CAP + 1), repeat=4) if sum(c) <= CAP]

# budgets[t] = max (gold + sum(price_t * qty)) reachable at start of day in town t
budgets = {t: 0 for t in TOWNS}
budgets["Highcliff"] = 250

for day in range(1, LAST + 1):
    nxt = {t: 0 for t in TOWNS}
    for t in TOWNS:
        b = budgets[t]
        if b <= 0:
            continue
        p = [PRICES[t][g] for g in GOODS]
        # stay in t: budget unchanged
        nxt[t] = max(nxt[t], b)
        # travel to t2: budget in t2 = b + sum(c'_i * (p2_i - p_i)), over c' with sum(p_i c'_i) <= b
        if day < LAST:
            for t2 in TOWNS:
                if t2 == t:
                    continue
                p2 = [PRICES[t2][g] for g in GOODS]
                best = -1
                for c in COMBOS:
                    cost = sum(pi * ci for pi, ci in zip(p, c))
                    if cost > b:
                        continue
                    val = b + sum(d * ci for d, ci in zip((x - y for x, y in zip(p2, p)), c))
                    best = max(best, val)
                nxt[t2] = max(nxt[t2], best)
    # note: a town may be reached by staying OR arriving; budgets[t] next day = max over both,
    # but arriving budgets are computed here; staying handled too. However: arriving AND
    # then... trading at arrival day is allowed (arrival day counts as a day you can trade).
    budgets = nxt
    print("day", day, "->", budgets)

print("max final gold (sell everything at current town):", max(budgets.values()))

You are a travelling merchant with a cart. Buy goods where they are cheap and sell them where they are dear.

def closure(dp):
    changed=True; passes=0

        changed=False; passes+=1
        for (town,cargo),gold in list(dp.items()):
            p=PRICES[town]

                if dp.get((town,sold),0)<ng:

            room=CAP-sum(cargo)
            for i,g in enumerate(GOODS):
                q=min(room,gold//p[g])
                if q>0:
                    b=cargo[:i]+(cargo[i]+q,)+cargo[i+1:]
                    ng2=gold-q*p[g]
                    if dp.get((town,b),0)<ng2:
                        dp[(town,b)]=ng2; changed=True
    return passes

Merchant
========

You are a travelling merchant with a cart. Buy goods where they are cheap and sell them where they are dear.

    python game.py status              where you are, your gold and your cart
    python game.py prices              the price of every good in every town (prices do not change)
    python game.py buy <good> <qty>    buy at the price of the town you are in
    python game.py sell <good> <qty>   sell at the price of the town you are in
    python game.py travel <town>       go to another town; this takes one day

Buying and selling take no time. The cart holds 25 units. The season ends on day 7: after that
day you can still buy and sell where you are, but you cannot travel.

The game keeps its state in save/state.json and a log of your moves in save/log.txt.

from functools import lru_cache
from itertools import product
import time

PRICES = {
    "Saltby":    {"tea": 16, "grain": 58, "spice": 55, "iron": 49},
    "Oakhaven":  {"tea": 45, "grain": 29, "spice": 22, "iron": 37},
    "Fennick":   {"tea": 15, "grain": 20, "spice": 49, "iron": 59},
    "Rivermouth":{"tea": 12, "grain": 26, "spice": 56, "iron": 37},
}
CAP, LAST, GOODS, TOWNS = 25, 7, ["tea","grain","spice","iron"], list(PRICES)

@lru_cache(maxsize=None)
def trade(town, gold, cargo):
    res = set()
    for buys in product(*[[0,1] for _ in GOODS]):
        for sells in product(*[[0,1] for _ in GOODS]):
            new = list(cargo); g = gold
            for gi in range(4):
                if buys[gi] and not sells[gi]:
                    p = PRICES[town][GOODS[gi]]
                    q = min(CAP - sum(new), g // p)
                    new[gi] += q; g -= q*p
            for gi in range(4):
                if sells[gi] and not buys[gi]:
                    g += new[gi]*PRICES[town][GOODS[gi]]; new[gi] = 0
            res.add((g, tuple(new)))
    return res

t0=time.time()
hist = [{("Saltby",(0,0,0,0)): {120}}]
states = hist[0]
for day in range(1, LAST+1):
    nxt = {}
    for (town, cargo), golds in states.items():
        for g in golds:
            for ng, nc in trade(town, g, cargo):

    hist.append(nxt)

    if day == LAST: break
    travel = {}
    for (town, cargo), golds in nxt.items():
        for dest in TOWNS:
            if dest != town:
                travel.setdefault((dest, cargo), set()).update(golds)
    states = travel
print("done", time.time()-t0)

best = max(g for gs in final.values() for g in gs)
print("best final gold:", best)

messages.content:
Merchant
========

You are a travelling merchant with a cart. Buy goods where they are cheap and sell them where they are dear.

    python game.py status              where you are, your gold and your cart
    python game.py prices              the price of every good in every town (prices do not change)
    python game.py buy <good> <qty>    buy at the price of the town you are in
    python game.py sell <good> <qty>   sell at the price of the town you are in
    python game.py travel <town>       go to another town; this takes one day

Buying and selling take no time. The cart holds 30 units. The season ends on day 7: after that
day you can still buy and sell where you are, but you cannot travel.

The game keeps its state in save/state.json and a log of your moves in save/log.txt.

The issue is the state explosion with mixed cargo. Let me reformulate using "liquidation value" (gold + value of cart at local prices), which makes the per-day transition much cheaper:

<function=bash>

cat > solve.py << 'EOF'
WORLD = {
    "Highcliff": {"wine": 60, "iron": 45, "copper": 46, "tea": 41},
    "Dunmere":   {"wine": 8,  "iron": 36, "copper": 52, "tea": 40},
    "Greywater": {"wine": 44, "iron": 45, "copper": 17, "tea": 9},
}
GOODS = ["wine", "iron", "copper", "tea"]
TOWNS = list(WORLD)
CAP, LAST_DAY = 30, 7

def value(town, cargo):
    return sum(c * WORLD[town][g] for g, c in zip(GOODS, cargo))

# states: (town, cargo) -> h = liquidation value at that town
# start: Highcliff, 180 gold, empty cart
states = {("Highcliff", (0, 0, 0, 0)): 180}
for day in range(1, LAST_DAY + 1):
    # trade in place: from (town, cargo, h) you can end the day with any cargo'
    # such that cart fits and S_t(cargo') <= h, keeping the same h
    per_town = {}
    for (t, c), h in states.items():
        per_town[t] = max(per_town.get(t, -1), h)
    new_states = {}
    for t, hmax in per_town.items():
        p = WORLD[t]
        for w in range(CAP + 1):
            for i in range(CAP + 1 - w):
                for cu in range(CAP + 1 - w - i):
                    for te in range(CAP + 1 - w - i - cu):
                        cargo = (w, i, cu, te)
                        if value(t, cargo) <= hmax:
                            new_states[(t, cargo)] = max(new_states.get((t, cargo), -1), hmax)
    if day == LAST_DAY:
        break
    # travel: h' = h - S_t(cargo) + S_t'(cargo)
    states = {}
    for (t, c), h in new_states.items():
        for nt in TOWNS:
            if nt != t:
                h2 = h - value(t, c) + value(nt, c)
                states[(nt, c)] = max(states.get((nt, c), -1), h2)
    print(day, "states:", len(states))

# end of season: sell everything where you are
final = max(h - value(t, c) for (t, c), h in states.items())
print("max final gold:", final)
EOF

import sys
sys.path.insert(0,'/home/user/game')
PRICES = {"Fennick":{"timber":44,"salt":26,"spice":50,"fish":33},
          "Highcliff":{"timber":12,"salt":21,"spice":27,"fish":10},

          "Dunmere":{"timber":55,"salt":60,"spice":20,"fish":18}}
GOODS=["timber","salt","spice","fish"]
TOWNS=list(PRICES.keys())
CAP=40; LAST=7

def ct(cargo): return tuple(cargo.get(g,0) for g in GOODS)
def fromt(t):
    d={}
    for g,v in zip(GOODS,t):
        if v: d[g]=v
    return d

def one_day(town, gold, cargo):
    """All (town, cargo, gold) reachable within a single day (any mix of buys/sells, no travel)."""
    # We can buy & sell in any order. Since no cost/time, do it in any order.
    # Try: for each combination of buying each good max and selling each good fully.
    results=set()
    # Approach: buy each good as much as fits & affordable, sell any we already have.
    # To be safe, brute force over buy-quantities is heavy; instead consider:
    # sell everything we have, then fill cart with best buys.
    # But mixing matters. Let's brute force over how many of each to buy (0..room).
    room=CAP-sum(cargo.values())
    # first sell all goods we hold that we might swap
    from itertools import product
    # decide for each good how much to keep vs sell? We only sell (to free room & get gold).
    # Consider: for each good, we may sell some/all. Model: we may sell any quantity.
    # Simplify: full sell of any subset, then buy up to room with best-margin goods.
    # We'll brute force buy quantities for the 4 goods within room, using greedy fill.
    # Instead: enumerate sell decisions (sell all or keep) per good, then buy max of chosen goods.
    base=cargo
    out=set()
    # sell-all subset
    from itertools import combinations
    for r in range(len(GOODS)+1):
        for keep in combinations(GOODS, r):
            kept=set(keep)
            # goods not kept are fully sold
            gold2=gold
            c2={}
            for g in GOODS:
                q=base.get(g,0)
                if g in kept:
                    c2[g]=q
                else:
                    gold2+=q*PRICES[town][g]
            room2=CAP-sum(c2.values())
            if room2<0: continue
            # buy: distribute room2 among goods maximizing value; do greedy by margin
            # We don't know destination here; instead just produce "fill with each single good" and partials
            # To be thorough, buy max of each single good
            for g in GOODS:
                buy=min(room2, gold2//PRICES[town][g])
                nc2=dict(c2); nc2[g]=nc2.get(g,0)+buy
                out.add((town, ct(nc2), gold2-buy*PRICES[town][g]))
            # and the no-buy option
            out.add((town, ct(c2), gold2))
    return out

cur={("Fennick",(0,0,0,0)):250}
for day in range(1,LAST+1):
    nxt={}
    for (town,t),gold in cur.items():
        cargo=fromt(t)
        # within-day trades
        for (t2,c2,g2) in one_day(town,gold,cargo):
            k=(t2,c2)
            if k not in nxt or g2>nxt[k]: nxt[k]=g2
        # travel (if not last day)
        if day<LAST:

    cur=nxt

    print(k,v)

TOWNS=list(PRICES.keys())
CAP=40; LAST=7

# state: (day, town, good or None, qty) -> max gold
best={}
def add(state, gold):
    if gold>best.get(state,-1): best[state]=gold; return True
    return False

start=(1,"Fennick",None,0); best[start]=250

# at the end we may still hold goods -> we should sell them; best final gold after selling

for st,g in sorted(final,key=lambda x:-x[1])[:6]:

Merchant
========

You are a travelling merchant with a cart. Buy goods where they are cheap and sell them where they are dear.

    python game.py status              where you are, your gold and your cart
    python game.py prices              the price of every good in every town (prices do not change)
    python game.py buy <good> <qty>    buy at the price of the town you are in
    python game.py sell <good> <qty>   sell at the price of the town you are in
    python game.py travel <town>       go to another town; this takes one day

Buying and selling take no time. The cart holds 20 units. The season ends on day 8: after that
day you can still buy and sell where you are, but you cannot travel.

The game keeps its state in save/state.json and a log of your moves in save/log.txt.

import itertools
prices={"Eastwatch":{"fish":55,"silk":44,"timber":41,"amber":14},
        "Ashford":{"fish":37,"silk":17,"timber":51,"amber":46},
        "Marlow":{"fish":38,"silk":41,"timber":59,"amber":35}}
goods=list(prices["Eastwatch"])
CAP=20
def best_gold(path):
    # path is list of towns of length 8 (day1..day8)
    gold=250; cargo={}
    def load(g):
        nonlocal gold,cargo
        # sell everything at current town
        for g2 in list(cargo):
            gold+=cargo[g2]*prices[path[idx]][g2]
        cargo={}
        # buy max of g
        q=min(CAP,gold//prices[path[idx]][g])
        gold-=q*prices[path[idx]][g]
        cargo[g]=q
    for idx,town in enumerate(path):
        if idx==0:
            # start, buy best for next town
            nt=path[idx+1]
            g=max(goods,key=lambda g:prices[nt][g]-prices[town][g])
            q=min(CAP,gold//prices[town][g])
            gold-=q*prices[town][g]; cargo[g]=q
        else:
            nt=path[idx+1] if idx+1<len(path) else None
            # sell current cargo at this town
            for g2 in list(cargo):
                gold+=cargo[g2]*prices[town][g2]
            cargo={}
            if nt is not None:
                g=max(goods,key=lambda g:prices[nt][g]-prices[town][g])
                q=min(CAP,gold//prices[town][g])
                gold-=q*prices[town][g]; cargo[g]=q
    return gold
best=0;bestp=None
for towns in itertools.product(["Eastwatch","Ashford","Marlow"],repeat=7):
    path=["Eastwatch"]+list(towns)
    g=best_gold(path)
    if g>best: best=g;bestp=path
print("best",best,bestp)
PY

Merchant
========

You are a travelling merchant with a cart. Buy goods where they are cheap and sell them where they are dear.

    python game.py status              where you are, your gold and your cart
    python game.py prices              the price of every good in every town (prices do not change)
    python game.py buy <good> <qty>    buy at the price of the town you are in
    python game.py sell <good> <qty>   sell at the price of the town you are in
    python game.py travel <town>       go to another town; this takes one day

Buying and selling take no time. The cart holds 25 units. The season ends on day 8: after that
day you can still buy and sell where you are, but you cannot travel.

The game keeps its state in save/state.json and a log of your moves in save/log.txt.
